newsitem.title: GERMANY: BDI head sees German welfare cuts needed - paper.
newsitem.headline: BDI head sees German welfare cuts needed - paper.

text.p: Germany will have to make further cuts in its social welfare system, Hans-Olaf Henkel, president of the Federation of German Industry, said.

The government's Program for More Jobs and Growth was a good beginning, but "a little more has to happen" before companies will be ready to invest to create new jobs, Henkel said in an interview with the newspaper Tageszeitung.
The interview is to be published on Monday, but advance copies were made available by the newspaper.
Market mechanisms could help save more in the health-care and insurance sectors without diminishing service, he said.
European monetary union will lead to a levelling of social standards, but not necessarily on the level of Germany, he said.
With unemployment of 10 percent, the German system is not really to be recommended to others, he said. Britain, Sweden and Portugal have been more successful at fighting unemployment, he said.
